nodes.name: Source
nodes.description: Undivided origin and possibility from which differentiation emerges.

nodes.name: Father
nodes.description: Upper/source principle associated with origin, verticality and the Father's House.

nodes.name: Father's House
nodes.description: Interior center of integration where scattered signals become an ordered whole.

nodes.name: Heaven
nodes.description: Upper domain of integration, clarity, unity, relationship, truth and love within the symbolic architecture.

nodes.name: Throne of North
nodes.description: Ultimate orientation point in the North Axis symbolism; symbolic rather than a claim of political sovereignty.

nodes.name: Ladder
nodes.description: Traversable vertical connection between levels, representing ascent, transformation and relationship.

nodes.name: Axis
nodes.description: Vertical organizing principle that gives the horizontal Plane orientation.

nodes.name: Door
nodes.description: Threshold, access, choice and interface between states; centrally coupled to the Son.

nodes.name: Narrow Gate
nodes.description: The constrained passage into transformation; a more specific expression of the Door.

nodes.name: Vessel
nodes.description: Container or carrier through which something from one layer can enter another.

nodes.name: Pineal Gland
nodes.description: Body-based metaphor used in the framework for the Door as an interface of perception; not presented as a scientific identification of a gland with a metaphysical portal.

nodes.name: Son
nodes.description: Person-bearing centre of the story, coupled to Thomas, Twin, Lion, Jesus Christ, Son of Man and Lion of Judah within the framework.

nodes.name: Thomas
nodes.description: Name attached to the Son/Twin identity in the Potatoverse story.

nodes.name: Twin
nodes.description: Duality and recognition motif attached to the Son.

nodes.name: Lion
nodes.description: Strength, kingship and identity motif attached to the Son.

nodes.name: Lion of Judah
nodes.description: Biblical/religious title used as a symbolic identity within the Son branch.

nodes.name: Jesus Christ
nodes.description: Christian symbolic identity mapped into the Son/Death/Door transformation architecture.

nodes.name: Son of Man
nodes.description: Religious title incorporated into the Son branch of the archive.

nodes.name: Death
nodes.description: Boundary event in the Son transformation sequence.

nodes.name: Crucifixion
nodes.description: Transformation point in which the Son's death becomes the symbolic bridge toward Door and Ladder.

nodes.name: Christmas
nodes.description: December 25 setting used in the Potatoverse timeline for the Son's death and Tim Dooley's mythic birth/transformation point.

nodes.name: North Pole
nodes.description: Polar location used as the meeting point of the Christmas, crucifixion and North Axis imagery.

nodes.name: Transformation
nodes.description: Process by which death, identity and symbolic function change into another form.

nodes.name: Tree of Life
nodes.description: Living expression of the Axis: roots, trunk, branches, leaves, fruit and seed model continuity and renewal.

nodes.name: Roots
nodes.description: Hidden substrate of origin, memory, ancestry, history, potential and matter.

nodes.name: Trunk
nodes.description: Continuity-bearing central body joining roots to branches.

nodes.name: Branches
nodes.description: Differentiating paths that emerge from one living axis.

nodes.name: Leaves
nodes.description: Visible expressions of the tree's life and contact with the surrounding world.

nodes.name: Fruit
nodes.description: Manifestation: what the living structure actually produces in the world.

nodes.name: Seed
nodes.description: Renewal and the possibility of another cycle.

nodes.name: Tree of Strife
nodes.description: Fractured tree pattern in which relationship is replaced by fear, competition, extraction and conflict.

nodes.name: Strife
nodes.description: Conflict generated when relationships cease to produce mutual life and instead produce domination, fear or fragmentation.

nodes.name: Swamp
nodes.description: Accumulated dysfunction, extraction, corruption, inertia, fear and systems that consume the life they should serve.

nodes.name: Mud
nodes.description: Ground-level material condition from which the Potato rises; also the metaphorical substrate of difficult beginnings.

nodes.name: Drain
nodes.description: Pattern in which energy, attention, resources or life are continuously pulled away without renewal.

nodes.name: Fear
nodes.description: Contraction force that can preserve life but can also become a driver of isolation and control.

nodes.name: Anger
nodes.description: High-energy response to perceived injury or injustice; potentially destructive or transformative depending on its direction.

nodes.name: Exploitation
nodes.description: Extraction of value, labour, attention or resources without a reciprocal structure that sustains the source.

nodes.name: Fragmentation
nodes.description: Loss of coherence between parts that could otherwise form a functioning whole.

nodes.name: Potato of Life
nodes.description: Central Potatoverse symbol for life emerging from ordinary matter, persistence, nourishment and transformation.

nodes.name: Potatoism
nodes.description: Potato-centered interpretive framework using ordinary matter, humor and growth from mud to examine life, identity and systems.

nodes.name: Red Potato
nodes.description: Creative, loving, expansive and upward/outward-moving life principle.

nodes.name: Blue Potato
nodes.description: Memory, precision, contraction and rootward movement; complementary to the Red Potato.

nodes.name: Spudlight
nodes.description: Light emerging through the Potato metaphor: illumination carried by ordinary, grounded life.

nodes.name: Potato Bank
nodes.description: Humorous financial metaphor for storing, circulating and accounting for value within the Potatoverse.

nodes.name: Cube
nodes.description: Container/order metaphor representing bounded space, structure and the world as an organized object.

nodes.name: Moon Cube
nodes.description: Extended Cube image used to explore remote, reflective and cyclical dimensions of the architecture.

nodes.name: North
nodes.description: Orientation toward the North Axis and geographic north as a project anchor.

nodes.name: South
nodes.description: Descent, material return and lower-field movement in the symbolic coordinate system.

nodes.name: East
nodes.description: Emergence, beginning, sunrise and outward becoming.

nodes.name: West
nodes.description: Completion, sunset, decline and return.

nodes.name: North Axis
nodes.description: Organizing northward direction connecting the symbolic Axis to a geographic and policy architecture.

nodes.name: Plane
nodes.description: Horizontal field where bodies, geography, society, institutions, technology, money, infrastructure and history become observable.

nodes.name: Matter
nodes.description: Physical substrate of the world: material objects, energy, substances and built environments.

nodes.name: Biology
nodes.description: Living systems, organisms, reproduction, ecology and the physical processes that sustain life.

nodes.name: People
nodes.description: Human beings as biological, social, economic, cultural and political participants.

nodes.name: Families
nodes.description: Primary social relationships through which care, inheritance, identity and intergenerational memory move.

nodes.name: Animals
nodes.description: Non-human life within ecosystems, agriculture, households, economies and human-animal relationships.

nodes.name: Places
nodes.description: Geographic locations that anchor events, infrastructure, communities, resources and institutions.

nodes.name: Nations
nodes.description: States and political communities with territory, institutions, laws, budgets, populations and external relationships.

nodes.name: Kingdoms
nodes.description: Political structures organized around a crown or monarchic constitutional tradition.

nodes.name: Societies
nodes.description: Networks of people, norms, institutions, culture, production and collective organization.

nodes.name: Institutions
nodes.description: Organizations and rule systems that coordinate authority, resources, law and public action.

nodes.name: Laws
nodes.description: Formal rules that allocate rights, duties, authority, property and permissible action.

nodes.name: Economies
nodes.description: Production, consumption, investment, employment, trade, finance and allocation of resources.

nodes.name: Technology
nodes.description: Tools, software, machines, networks and technical capabilities that alter productive and social capacity.

nodes.name: Infrastructure
nodes.description: Physical and digital networks that allow people and economies to function: power, transport, ports, cables, water and communications.

nodes.name: History
nodes.description: Recorded sequence of events, institutions, conflicts, transformations and inherited conditions.

nodes.name: War
nodes.description: Organized political violence with military, economic, industrial, demographic and infrastructural consequences.

nodes.name: Trade
nodes.description: Cross-border exchange of goods and services through markets, contracts, logistics and rules.

nodes.name: Money
nodes.description: Unit of account, medium of exchange and store of value connecting households, firms, states and financial systems.

nodes.name: Ownership & Control
nodes.description: Legal or effective control over companies, assets, land, infrastructure, intellectual property and financial claims.

nodes.name: Obligations
nodes.description: Debts, contracts, guarantees, pensions, taxes, legal duties and other claims that bind one actor to another.

nodes.name: Alliances
nodes.description: Formal or durable security, political and economic relationships among states and institutions.

nodes.name: European Economic Graph
nodes.description: Relationship-first map of European states, companies, ownership, debt, finance, energy, infrastructure, trade, technology, research, labour and strategic dependencies.

nodes.name: North Programme
nodes.description: Applied framework for fiscal sustainability, productive investment, industrial capacity, energy security, infrastructure, technology, research, labour and voluntary European cooperation.

nodes.name: European Union
nodes.description: Political and economic union connecting 27 member states through common institutions and the single market.

nodes.name: EU Single Market
nodes.description: Economic integration framework based on free movement of goods, services, capital and people.

nodes.name: Euro Area
nodes.description: Monetary union of EU member states using the euro, with shared monetary policy under the Eurosystem.

nodes.name: European Central Bank
nodes.description: Central institution of the Eurosystem responsible for euro-area monetary policy and financial-system functions.

nodes.name: Denmark
nodes.description: EU member state and northern anchor node in the working North Axis architecture.

nodes.name: Kingdom of Denmark
nodes.description: Constitutional realm comprising Denmark, Greenland and the Faroe Islands.

nodes.name: Greenland
nodes.description: Autonomous part of the Kingdom of Denmark and a major Arctic geographic, resource and strategic node.

nodes.name: Faroe Islands
nodes.description: Self-governing part of the Kingdom of Denmark, linking North Atlantic geography, fisheries, shipping and security.

nodes.name: Canada
nodes.description: North American Arctic and Atlantic state forming a major western node of the broader North Atlantic architecture.

nodes.name: Iceland
nodes.description: North Atlantic state connecting Arctic, European, energy, shipping and transatlantic infrastructure systems.

nodes.name: Norway
nodes.description: North Atlantic and Arctic state with major energy, maritime, fisheries and strategic infrastructure links to Europe.

nodes.name: Sweden
nodes.description: Nordic EU member with major industrial, technology, energy and Baltic-region connections.

nodes.name: Finland
nodes.description: Nordic EU member with Arctic, Baltic, industrial, technology and security connections.

nodes.name: United Kingdom
nodes.description: North Atlantic state whose finance, energy, security, shipping and trade links make it a major external node for European analysis.

nodes.name: Ukraine
nodes.description: European state whose war, reconstruction, energy, agriculture, industry and security relationships materially affect the European system.

nodes.name: Turkey
nodes.description: Transcontinental state connecting Europe, Black Sea, Caucasus, Middle East, transport corridors and energy routes.

nodes.name: Netherlands
nodes.description: EU economy with major ports, logistics, trade, energy, agriculture, finance and semiconductor-equipment connections.

nodes.name: France
nodes.description: Major EU economy and priority North Programme case for fiscal, industrial, energy and institutional research.

nodes.name: Belgium
nodes.description: EU member and priority North Programme case for fiscal, institutional, logistics and energy research.

nodes.name: North Sea
nodes.description: Shared maritime system connecting offshore wind, oil and gas, shipping, ports, fisheries, cables and coastal industry across several European states.

nodes.name: North Atlantic
nodes.description: Oceanic system connecting Europe, Greenland, Iceland, Norway, the UK and Canada through shipping, cables, fisheries, energy and security.

nodes.name: Arctic
nodes.description: Polar region where climate, shipping, resources, indigenous communities, research and security increasingly intersect.

nodes.name: European Energy System
nodes.description: Interlinked generation, grids, fuels, storage, markets and industrial demand across Europe.

nodes.name: European Electricity Grid
nodes.description: Cross-border transmission and distribution network linking generation, storage, industry and households.

nodes.name: Renewable Energy
nodes.description: Wind, solar, hydro and other renewable generation coupled to grids, storage and demand.

nodes.name: Nuclear Energy
nodes.description: Low-carbon electricity generation with long-lived infrastructure, fuel-cycle and regulatory requirements.

nodes.name: North Sea Offshore Wind
nodes.description: Offshore generation and associated grid, port, vessel and industrial supply chains in the North Sea.

nodes.name: European Ports
nodes.description: Maritime gateways where shipping, logistics, energy, industry and trade converge.

nodes.name: Subsea Cables
nodes.description: Electricity and telecommunications infrastructure connecting countries and markets beneath seas and oceans.

nodes.name: Finance & Public Debt
nodes.description: Bonds, banks, funds, public liabilities, monetary institutions and capital markets.

nodes.name: Public Debt
nodes.description: Outstanding government liabilities, including bonds and other borrowing used to finance public expenditure and investment.

nodes.name: Public Procurement
nodes.description: Government purchasing of goods, services and works; a major interface between public budgets and private production.

nodes.name: Pensions
nodes.description: Old-age income systems whose financing, demographics and labour-market incentives materially affect long-run public budgets.

nodes.name: Healthcare
nodes.description: Public and private systems providing prevention, treatment, hospitals, medicines, workforce and long-term care.

nodes.name: European Research System
nodes.description: Universities, institutes, public funding, industrial R&D and technology-transfer networks supporting knowledge production.

nodes.name: European Labour Market
nodes.description: Employment, wages, skills, migration, participation, training and productivity across European economies.

nodes.name: Semiconductor Supply Chain
nodes.description: Highly specialized chain spanning design, equipment, materials, fabrication, packaging and downstream electronics.

nodes.name: Cloud & AI Compute
nodes.description: Data centres, cloud platforms, accelerators, electricity and network infrastructure supporting modern digital services and AI.

nodes.name: European Industrial Base
nodes.description: Manufacturing capacity, machinery, chemicals, vehicles, aerospace, defence, pharmaceuticals and other productive capabilities.

nodes.name: Strategic Dependencies
nodes.description: External inputs or capabilities whose interruption could materially constrain European production, security or autonomy.

nodes.name: Cross
nodes.description: Intersection of Plane and Axis: the point where the horizontal world becomes vertically readable as root/consequence below and integration/source-facing orientation above.

nodes.name: Knowledge / Distinction
nodes.description: The differentiating act that creates distinction, memory, judgment, responsibility and choice; upstream of both Life and Strife rather than identical with either.

nodes.name: Roots of Strife
nodes.description: Unresolved buried material that reproduces conflict, dependency, capture or fragmentation rather than nourishing future growth.

nodes.name: Roots of Ash
nodes.description: Residue after destruction, severance, exhaustion or burning; a stored consequence that may remain inert or be metabolized into soil for later growth.

nodes.name: Living Root
nodes.description: Memory, history and consequence held in a relation capable of nourishing present continuity and future growth.

nodes.name: Wide Road
nodes.description: Outward/downward dispersive pathway in which repetition and widening become easier than integrative transformation; an operator/path rather than a D-level.

nodes.name: Repair
nodes.description: Return pathway that surfaces buried causes, distinguishes them, crosses a threshold, changes recurrence and converts residue into greater capacity for truthful or generative relation.

nodes.name: Gardener
nodes.description: Mature stewardship role: cultivate conditions for growth, protect, prune obstruction, repair soil and return integrated orientation to the Plane.

nodes.name: Tim Dooley
nodes.description: Central project subject and authorial/public identity whose biography, self-description, works and mythic roles are tracked separately from external verification.

nodes.name: Spiritual Domain
nodes.description: Project-symbolic upper/integrative domain used to group Father, Spirit, Heaven, Axis and related functions; not a literal physical location.

nodes.name: Dao De Jing
nodes.description: Classical Daoist text used only as a comparative textual neighbor for Source, Way, vessel and non-coercive order motifs.

nodes.name: Poetic Edda
nodes.description: Old Norse poetic corpus used comparatively for world-tree, roots, wells and cosmological structure.

nodes.name: Messianic Traditions
nodes.description: Jewish, Christian and other messianic traditions studied comparatively without collapsing them into the Potatoverse.

nodes.name: Christian Bible
nodes.description: Canonical Christian scriptures used as a primary textual context for Jesus, Son of Man, Door, Ladder and related comparative studies.

nodes.name: Torah / Tanakh
nodes.description: Hebrew Bible textual world used for Lion of Judah, Jacob's ladder, Eden, wisdom, kingship and other comparative motifs.

nodes.name: Acts of Thomas
nodes.description: Early Christian apocryphal Thomas tradition used as historical/comparative context for Judas Thomas.

nodes.name: Gospel of Thomas
nodes.description: Sayings gospel associated with Didymus Judas Thomas, used as a comparative textual source rather than proof of Potatoverse identity claims.

nodes.name: North Pole Christmas Myth
nodes.description: Project-specific cluster joining Christmas, North Pole, death/transformation and mythic birth motifs.

nodes.name: Potatoverse Epistemology
nodes.description: Framework for separating project canon, self-description, historical evidence, comparison, interpretation and inference.

nodes.name: Research
nodes.description: Open process of evidence gathering, comparison, modeling, testing, revision and source criticism across the project.

nodes.name: Son Transformation Cycle
nodes.description: Project sequence coupling ordeal, death, burial, Door, Ladder, return and renewed function on the Son side of the mythology.

nodes.name: Thomas / Son Study
nodes.description: Comparative study of the project Son/Thomas mapping against canonical and non-canonical Thomas traditions.

nodes.name: Thomas Textual Corpus
nodes.description: Grouped textual material relevant to Thomas traditions, including canonical and apocryphal sources, kept distinct by source and date.

nodes.name: Garden
nodes.description: Cultivated field of differentiated life where multiple branches can grow with nourishment, boundaries, passage and stewardship rather than forced sameness.

nodes.name: Rooms
nodes.description: Differentiated habitable spaces within a larger House/Garden architecture; plurality with relation, boundary and passage.

nodes.name: Mountain
nodes.description: Continuous-gradient image of ascent and integration: broad lower field compressing toward higher perspective, distinct from the Ladder's discrete thresholds.

nodes.name: Spiral
nodes.description: Recurrence with level-change: a return to related material in a changed state rather than a closed loop repeating at the same level.

nodes.name: Crown
nodes.description: Integrated summit perspective where many lower relations are evaluated together and are required to return as accountable service.

nodes.name: Burial
nodes.description: Hidden or protected placement below visible expression; may indicate loss, incubation, storage or the precondition for later emergence depending on context.

nodes.name: Eye
nodes.description: Perception, discernment and a latent generative aperture: the point at which a viable possibility can be noticed, evaluated and potentially activated.

nodes.name: Sprout
nodes.description: Activated visible growth trajectory emerging from stored capability or a latent eye; early direction before mature branching.

nodes.name: Return
nodes.description: Re-entry into the Plane or a prior thematic position carrying retained memory and changed capability; return is recurrence with a delta rather than reset.

nodes.name: Soil
nodes.description: Surrounding enabling conditions—resources, relationships, history, context and support—that can permit or constrain viable growth.

nodes.name: Forge
nodes.description: Bounded pressure intentionally transformed into transferable capability; successful only when the resulting capacity can survive after the pressure ends.

nodes.name: Dormancy
nodes.description: Viable regulated non-expression used biologically and symbolically for latent capability that is not currently growing visibly; not equivalent to death or failure.

nodes.name: Wound
nodes.description: Damage or broken continuity requiring protection, containment and repair before ordinary growth can safely resume.

nodes.name: Mature
nodes.description: Stable developed capability able to function without depending on the conditions that originally produced it.

nodes.name: Ash
nodes.description: Residue after rupture, destruction, burning or exhausted form; may remain inert, become Mud, enter a Forge, be archived, or become Soil.

nodes.name: Ring
nodes.description: Recurrence with approximately zero net change in capability or understanding; contrasted with Spiral as return carrying retained change.

nodes.name: House
nodes.description: Compositional whole preserving differentiated Dwellings/Rooms, boundaries, inhabitants and passage; the preferred ownership metaphor for the Potato House.

nodes.name: Dwelling
nodes.description: Major abiding domain inside a House; neutral structural term used to project the ten canonical top-level bounded contexts.

nodes.name: Mansions / Dwelling Places
nodes.description: Older English John 14:2 bridge for monai; retained as symbolic vocabulary while distinguished from modern luxury-house meaning and literal afterlife geography.

nodes.name: Chamber
nodes.description: Optional smaller specialist/protected cell inside a Room when a stable local task or boundary warrants it.

nodes.name: Court / Courtyard
nodes.description: Shared approach/common space serving several inner destinations before a more selective threshold.

nodes.name: Gate
nodes.description: Perimeter access regime controlling entry into a larger domain, city, garden or compound; broader than a local Door.

nodes.name: Foundation
nodes.description: Load-bearing invariant beneath later construction; used for constitutional, provenance and ownership supports.

nodes.name: Cornerstone
nodes.description: Alignment/reference element whose placement constrains the geometry of a larger structure; distinct from every other stone or builder role.

nodes.name: Pillar
nodes.description: Repeated vertical support that carries load while preserving open differentiated space around it.

nodes.name: Temple
nodes.description: Presence/access architecture joining foundation, building, sanctuary, service and dwelling; an alternate View, not a synonym for House ownership.

nodes.name: Sanctuary
nodes.description: Protected presence space with stronger access conditions than ordinary habitation.

nodes.name: City
nodes.description: Federated plurality at civic scale: many dwellings, gates, roads, institutions and participants sharing infrastructure.

nodes.name: Body
nodes.description: One coordinated organism composed of differentiated members/functions; emphasizes mutual dependence and functional specialization.

nodes.name: Vine
nodes.description: Living continuity supporting differentiated branches and fruit; an organic participation grammar distinct from House/City/Body.

nodes.name: Vineyard
nodes.description: Bounded productive field whose health is evaluated by fruit and treatment of entrusted life.

nodes.name: Treasury / Storehouse
nodes.description: Stored future capacity/resources retained for later use; distinct from Archive/provenance.

nodes.name: Archive
nodes.description: Preserved records and provenance enabling reconstruction, correction and historical continuity.

nodes.name: River / Stream
nodes.description: Flow distributing life, resources, information or capability through a larger structure.

nodes.name: Well / Spring
nodes.description: Local access point to a deeper or replenishing source.

nodes.name: Table
nodes.description: Shared place of participation, deliberation, exchange or distribution without collapsing distinct participants.

nodes.name: Tent / Tabernacle
nodes.description: Portable/provisional dwelling or presence architecture; useful project analogue for prototypes and migration layers before permanent promotion.

nodes.name: Throne / Seat
nodes.description: Orientation, judgment and responsibility point rather than a container; legitimacy is tested by accountable service and return.

nodes.name: Household
nodes.description: Participant ecology inhabiting or maintaining a House; distinct from the architecture and from universal ownership.

nodes.name: Commons
nodes.description: Shared capability/resource layer governed among multiple autonomous participants without requiring one participant to own the whole.

nodes.name: Network
nodes.description: Relation topology among autonomous nodes whose joint capabilities arise from roads, protocols, flows and dependencies.

nodes.name: Assembly / Council
nodes.description: Deliberative gathering for review, decision or coordination among distinct participants or representatives.

nodes.name: Kingdom / Realm
nodes.description: Normative or orientational scope of value, responsibility and order; project-symbolic use does not create civil sovereignty or legal jurisdiction.

nodes.name: Civilization
nodes.description: Long-duration emergent pattern formed by cities, networks, commons, institutions, infrastructures, memory and culture across generations.

nodes.name: Garden-City
nodes.description: City/federation regime combining dense coordination with regeneration, repairability and peripheral autonomy; project comparative model, not a literal identification of a modern polity with New Jerusalem.

nodes.name: Bridge
nodes.description: Connection that creates usable capability across an existing separation while preserving endpoint identity.

nodes.name: Protocol
nodes.description: Shared grammar or rules enabling heterogeneous nodes to interoperate without becoming identical or transferring ownership.
